items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: And then I’d be at the house hanging out with him and Keiko

ctx.x: Because I saw him once in a club and man, he looked furious, and he was sweating. And I was like sort of scared of that energy. So when I read that you played with him — and you followed some good — obviously some fantastic bass players over the years, so I was wondering what that felt like.

Man it was amazing. I mean it was surreal. Because I was young and I was playing with Elvin. And then he was like, “You need to move to New York.” And then I’d be at the house hanging out with him and Keiko, you know it was — first of all, even though he’s a big guy, when he’d lose his temper it was scary. But it would be about ten seconds and then he’d be like, “Ah I love you” and he’d hug you. So he was actually a very sweet man, very smart guy, quiet, once again, didn’t talk that much. But you know like he…
If an interviewer, you know, got an interview with him and opened the first thing they said was, “Mr. Jones tell us about John Coltrane.” How would be react to that?
